items.title: 8.2 Reversible reactions, microscopic waqiat aur dynamic equilibrium (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 8.2, printed pages 168-170.

blocks.text: Jab reversible reaction equilibrium par ho to bazahir lagta hai ke woh ruk gayi hai (static). Lekin microscopic level par reaction kabhi nahi rukti aur molecules musalsal badalte rehte hain. Reactant molecules products mein badalte hain, aur usi waqt ulta amal (reverse process) bhi ho raha hota hai. Is liye hum micro scale par dekhte hain ke kaun se waqiat system ki macroscopic properties par asar dalte hain.

Munasib halaat mein steam (pani ki bhaap) aur carbon monoxide ki reaction lein. In gases ko milane par macroscopic tabdeeliyan nazar aati hain (misal ke taur par concentration badalna). Farz karein dono reactants ke moles barabar le kar reaction shuru ki gayi. Milate hi in ke darmiyan har second sab se zyada collisions (takkar) hoti hain; yeh microscopic events hain. CO aur H₂O ke bonds tootte hain aur naye bonds ban kar H₂ aur CO₂ bante hain. Is liye shuru mein forward reaction ki rate sab se zyada hoti hai. Is se reactants ki concentration kam hoti hai. Jaise jaise H₂O aur CO kharch hote hain, forward reaction aahista ho jati hai.

Jab H₂ aur CO₂ ke molecules jama hone lagte hain to reverse reaction bhi shuru ho jati hai. H₂ aur CO₂ ki concentration barhne ke saath in molecules ke darmiyan har second ziada se ziada collisions hoti hain. H₂ aur CO₂ ke bonds tootte hain aur CO aur H₂O ke bonds bante hain.

blocks.alt: Waqt ke muqable concentration ka graph. Neela curve [CO] ya [H2O] oonchi jagah se shuru ho kar girta hai; magenta curve [CO2] ya [H2] sifar se uthta hai aur neele curve ko kaat-ta hai. Dashed khari lakeer 'Equilibrium' par dono curves seedhe (flat) ho jate hain, magenta neele se oopar.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.1: Waqt ke muqable concentration ka plot ([CO] ya [H2O] aur [CO2] ya [H2]) (kitab ki Figure 8.1 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Matlab forward reaction sab se tez rate se shuru ho kar aahista hoti jati hai, jabke reverse reaction ki rate shuru mein kam hoti hai, phir barhti hai aur aakhir mein constant ho jati hai.

blocks.alt: Hamara apna graph: waqt ke muqable rate. Surkh 'forward rate' oonchi jagah se girta hai, neela 'reverse rate' sifar se uthta hai; dashed lakeer par dono barabar ho kar ek seedhi lakeer ban jate hain (rates equal: equilibrium).
blocks.caption: H2O + CO ke liye forward aur reverse rates waqt ke saath (hamara apna khaaka; kitab mein yeh graph nahi).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Pehle graph (Figure 8.1) mein shuru mein sirf CO aur H₂O hain, is liye in ki concentration oonchi hai aur girti hai, jabke H₂ aur CO₂ zero se barhte hain. Dashed lakeer ke baad dono lakeerein seedhi (flat) hain: equilibrium par concentrations nahi badaltin. Doosra graph hamara apna hai aur wajah dikhata hai: forward rate girti hai, reverse rate barhti hai, aur jab dono barabar ho jati hain to equilibrium aa jata hai.

Aakhir kar aisa waqt aata hai jab dono reactions ek hi rate se chalti hain. Is stage par reaction chemical equilibrium mein hoti hai aur reactants aur products ki concentrations constant ho jati hain.
Jab tak system ko kisi tarah chheda (disturb) na jaye, concentrations mein mazeed koi tabdeeli nahi hoti.

blocks.title: Chemical equilibrium ki halat
blocks.text: Reversible reaction ki woh halat jis mein reaction mixture ki composition (banawat) nahi badalti aur forward aur reverse rates barabar hoti hain, chemical equilibrium ki halat kehlati hai.

Figure 8.1 mein ek aam reaction ke liye waqt (time) ke muqable reactants aur products ki concentrations ke graphs hain. Farz karein reactant A badal kar product B banta hai. Graphs dikhate hain ke equilibrium ke baad kya kya ho sakta hai: reactant aur product ki concentrations barabar ho sakti hain (Figure 8.1 a), ya reactant product se kam ya zyada ho sakta hai (Figure 8.1 b aur c). Lekin har graph mein saaf hai ke equilibrium ke baad concentrations constant ho jati hain.

blocks.alt: Teen graphs: waqt ke muqable reactant A (neela, girta hua) aur product B (magenta, uthta hua) ki concentration. Har graph mein dashed khari lakeer 'Equilibrium' ke baad dono curves seedhe hain. (a) A aur B barabar concentration par ruk jate hain. (b) A, B se neeche rukta hai. (c) A, B se oopar rukta hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.1: Waqt ke muqable concentration ka plot (a) Reactant = Product (b) Reactant < Product (c) Reactant > Product (kitab ki Figure 8.1 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Jab concentrations constant ho jayein to lagta hai ke reaction ruk gayi, lekin aisa nahi hai. Microscopic level par bohat sargarmi (activity) hai. Reactants ke molecules react karte rehte hain, aur products ke molecules bhi aapas mein mil kar wapas reactants bante rehte hain. Forward process ki rate reverse process ki rate ke bilkul barabar hai. Is liye ise dynamic equilibrium (harkat wala equilibrium) kehte hain: molecules musalsal react kar rahe hain, lekin dono rates ek jaisi hain.

items: H₂O + CO mein forward rate shuru mein sab se zyada hoti hai aur reactants kharch hone par girti hai; reverse rate zero se barhti hai.
Dono rates barabar hon to chemical equilibrium: composition constant rehti hai.
Equilibrium dynamic hai: molecules dono taraf react karte rehte hain, chahe aakhri concentrations barabar hon ya na hon.
